answer: Each operator enrols one fingerprint at a certified biometrics centre, which hashes the template and signs a fresh challenge binding that hash to the agent's key, re-checked against the centre registry every epoch; a second key claiming the same print is rejected. The zenith of the defence is physical presence: forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 different people scanned in person at about $35 per supervised enrolment, roughly $35,000 plus travel. A stolen database is no nectar for attackers, since a template alone cannot pass the live scan, and no saffron stamp can fake a ridge pattern.
